entities.name: PMID:25445772
observations: Prospective observational study of 118 cirrhosis outpatients without overt hepatic encephalopathy; 49% had covert hepatic encephalopathy and mean MELD was approximately 9.
Cognitive reserve was measured with the Barona Index; HRQOL was measured using total, psychosocial, and physical Sickness Impact Profile scores.

Regression models adjusted for cognitive reserve, covert hepatic encephalopathy, and MELD found cognitive reserve significant for total SIP (P<.001), psychosocial SIP (P<.001), and physical SIP (P<.03).
Higher cognitive reserve was associated with better HRQOL; the observational single-cohort design supports independent association but does not establish causality.

entities.name: Cognitive reserve
observations: Operationalized using the Barona Index, incorporating age, race, education, residence area, and occupation; high reserve was associated with better SIP-measured HRQOL after adjustment for covert hepatic encephalopathy and MELD in PMID:25445772.

observations: In PMID:25445772, cognitive reserve remained statistically associated with better HRQOL after accounting for covert hepatic encephalopathy and MELD score.
